Tessa / Laura / Olga,

I've drafted an options matrix and attached two artifacts (ip-decision-matrix.xlsx, procurement-notes.pdf). High-level recommendation below to keep the deal moving while protecting Redwood:

Option A (Client assignment) — Accept assignment of Outputs to customer
  - Pros: clears customer's procurement path
  - Cons: blocks Redwood from using outputs to build features; hard to quantify long-term cost
  - Risk: High (loss of reuse)

Option B (Exclusive field-limited license for Customer + Redwood feedback carve-out) — Recommended
  - Language: "Customer is granted exclusive rights to use Outputs for its internal and commercial productization in the Field of Use specified in the Order Form. Redwood retains a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and to use Customer Feedback for model and service improvements, provided no Customer Prompt or Output is used to train models without Customer's prior written opt-in."
  - Pros: balances customer's need for productization with Redwood's need to iterate/improve
  - Cons: Novum may push on 'exclusive' scope; needs precise Field of Use
  - Risk: Moderate

Option C (Customer owns Outputs + pay extra for carve-out) — commercial trade
  - Pros: meets customer's ask
  - Cons: revenue tradeoff to offset IP loss

Action items for legal: provide precise snippet for Section X (Output Rights) and a short clause for Training & Feedback (we can reuse standard opt-in language).

If we go with Option B, procurement should offer a 10% discount on committed monthly usage over 12 months in exchange for Redwood's retained feedback license.

Hi Evan,

Thanks for the redline and for the clarity on Novum's needs. After internal review we want to propose a compromise to keep you moving toward approval:

Proposed (summary):
- Outputs: Customer will receive exclusive rights to use Outputs for the Field of Use defined in the Order Form. This is not an assignment of all IP in perpetuity — Redwood retains ownership of the underlying models and tooling.
- Training & Data Use: Redwood will not use Customer Prompts or Outputs to train models without explicit, written opt-in. Redwood may collect aggregated, de-identified telemetry and use Customer Feedback (bug reports, reproducible examples) to improve service quality and models. We will not link de-identified telemetry back to Customer identities.
- Commercial trade: In exchange for Redwood's retained feedback/license carve-out, we can provide a 10% discount on committed usage for the first 12 months and an SLA commitment of 99.9% for production routes.

I have attached a redline (ip-decision-matrix.xlsx contains suggested language snippets) and a one-page summary (procurement-notes.pdf).
